nodes.label: Unknown-step task direction — 2026-11-09
nodes.status: Task selected; runtime, simulation, training and hardware runs not released

nodes.label: Unknown-step traversal, tracking, goal and stop
nodes.summary: User-selected priority: traverse a mechanically feasible unknown step, reach the physical goal and stop; then assess path tracking and completion time. Replaces known-step vibration preview. The six MQ draft slots had zero allocation.
nodes.rationale: Vibration, discrepancy and saturation are secondary diagnostics; holding nominal speed or reducing vibration alone does not establish task completion.

nodes.label: Deployable controller versus privileged scoring boundary
nodes.summary: Controller may know route and goal and use causal IMU, wheel encoders, command history, freshness and estimator. Step position, geometry, contact schedule and GT remain in separate scoring/audit channels. Start with 20 features × 5 frames; omit Common103 planned-stop features.
nodes.rationale: IMU/encoder disturbance signals arrive after physical interaction begins; they are neither preview nor ground-truth first contact.

nodes.label: Physical success, explicit failure and UNKNOWN
nodes.summary: Success requires body arrival, full-robot geometric clearance and continuous stop. Keep failure, timeout, stall and override in the denominator; missing measurement is UNKNOWN. Report outcomes before tracking/time. Numeric tolerances and budget remained unset.
nodes.rationale: Estimator arrival and aggregate reward cannot substitute for physical task success or conceal failure.

nodes.label: Hidden development/validation/test layout bank
nodes.summary: Begin with the rigid Ø6 mm development family; vary hidden position and include clear floor. Lock splits by complete run/layout/seed before checkpoint selection. Test that changing obstacle metadata with identical sensor history leaves controller packets unchanged.
nodes.rationale: A fixed step position can be learned from elapsed time or progress even without an obstacle_x feature. Feature-name guards alone do not prove provenance or remove shortcuts.

nodes.label: B0, reactive B1, history and residual TD3 roles
nodes.summary: B0 is the unknown-step follower plus velocity backend and limits. B1 uses causal sensors/history and requires separate qualification. Residual TD3 is a bounded velocity-reference candidate after task/environment validation; PPO is optional. Qualify the environment before optimizer work, then compare trained policies against appropriate baselines.
nodes.rationale: An untrained TD3 policy need not beat classical control before training, and a smoke run cannot establish convergence or learned benefit.
